name: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
tagline: Managed Kubernetes: Azure runs the control plane, you run the workloads.
whatItIs: A managed Kubernetes service. Azure hosts, patches and scales the Kubernetes control plane; your applications run on node pools — Virtual Machine Scale Sets in your subscription — that you size and scale. AKS integrates with Entra ID, Azure networking, storage, Container Registry and Azure Monitor.
primaryPurpose: Run containerized applications at scale with the full Kubernetes API and ecosystem, without operating the control plane yourself.
useCases: Microservice platforms with many services, custom scheduling or service meshes
Teams standardizing on Kubernetes tooling (Helm, GitOps, operators) across environments
Lift-and-shift of existing Kubernetes workloads from on-premises or other clouds
Batch, data and AI/ML workloads on GPU or Spot node pools
keyFeatures: Managed control plane with Free, Standard (uptime SLA) and Premium (long-term support) tiers
Multiple node pools: Linux and Windows, GPU, Spot, availability zones
Cluster autoscaler, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, KEDA and node auto-provisioning
Networking models including Azure CNI Overlay and Azure CNI powered by Cilium
Entra ID integration, Azure RBAC for Kubernetes, Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Auto-upgrade channels and planned maintenance windows
AKS Automatic: an opinionated, more fully managed cluster configuration
security: Integrate with Microsoft Entra ID, disable local accounts, and use Azure RBAC or Kubernetes RBAC
Use Workload ID for pod access to Azure resources — no secrets in the cluster
Restrict the API server with a private cluster or authorized IP ranges
Enforce guardrails with the Azure Policy add-on; protect with Microsoft Defender for Containers
networking: Choose a network model: Azure CNI Overlay (pod IPs from a private overlay range, conserving VNet space), Azure CNI with VNet-routable pod IPs, or Cilium-powered dataplane
Services of type LoadBalancer configure an Azure Standard Load Balancer (public or internal)
Ingress via the application routing add-on (managed NGINX) or Application Gateway for Containers
Network policies (Azure, Calico or Cilium) control pod-to-pod traffic
pricing: The control plane is free on the Free tier; Standard and Premium tiers add a per-cluster hourly charge. You pay separately for node VMs, disks, load balancers, public IPs, bandwidth and monitoring. Reservations, savings plans and Spot node pools reduce node costs.

confusedWith.name: Azure Container Apps
confusedWith.difference: Serverless containers built on Kubernetes with no cluster to manage; AKS exposes the full Kubernetes API and operations.

confusedWith.name: Azure Container Instances
confusedWith.difference: Single container groups on demand without orchestration; AKS orchestrates fleets of containers.

confusedWith.name: Azure Red Hat OpenShift
confusedWith.difference: A jointly managed OpenShift (Kubernetes distribution) service; AKS is Microsoft's upstream-Kubernetes offering.

relevanceNote: Not in the AZ-104 skills outline — included for wider context. On the exam, prefer ACI or Container Apps when they meet the requirement with less administrative effort.
examTips: If an AZ-104 question needs a simple container with minimal management, AKS is usually the distractor
Azure manages the control plane; you manage node pools, workloads and upgrades
versionNote: Tiers, SKUs and networking options change frequently; confirm on the AKS documentation and pricing pages.
